title: She lights it
logline: The Fourth: no fireworks again, and Gully's daughter, fifteen, at the dock's end with the one firework and the lighter and her mother's nod. The one white burst, from the steps. A knee and a hand.

panels.composition: From the shack steps: a fifteen-year-old girl at the dock's end lighting a single firework, her mother in the lawn chair giving the tiny nod, her father with his arms folded, the pup barking at the first spark; at the page's bottom edge a knee and a hand. The sky still dark.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, seen from shack steps, a teenage girl at the end of a dock lighting a single firework while a woman in an old lawn chair nods and a heavy man stands with his arms folded, a small three-legged dog barking at the spark, a man's knee and hand at the page's bottom edge, dark sky, no words

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: She lights it. The nod, passed down.
